claims.text: Equiatomic FeNiCrMn has an FCC single-crystal initial structure under the modeled conditions.
Dynamic deformation under uniaxial tension in single-crystal equiatomic FCC FeNiCrMn is dominated by vacancy-induced dislocation nucleation.
Vacancy clusters or disordered atoms act as dislocation-nucleation sites.
Nucleation at these sites emits Shockley partial dislocations with Burgers vectors of the 1/6<112> type.
The emitted Shockley partials generate intrinsic and extrinsic stacking faults.
The stacking faults produce local HCP-like regions.
Yielding is marked by a sudden stress drop coincident with dislocation nucleation at vacancy sites.
Increasing temperature intensifies atomic thermal vibrations and facilitates dislocation nucleation.
Increasing temperature lowers the critical resolved shear stress and yield strength.
Increasing strain rate raises dislocation density because kinetic limitations suppress dislocation annihilation.
Yield strength is negligibly sensitive to strain rate from 10^8 to 10^10 s^-1.
The <-111> tensile-loading direction produces the maximum yield stress among the tested orientations.
No FCC-to-BCC transformation occurs under the tested conditions.
No deformation twinning occurs under the tested conditions.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to single-crystal FCC FeNiCrMn under tensile loading at strain rates from 10^8 to 10^10 s^-1.
The proposed mechanism does not purport to describe polycrystalline behavior, twinning-dominated deformation, or bulk phase transformations.
DXA and CNA can be used to test whether yielding coincides with vacancy-associated dislocation nucleation and stacking-fault formation.
Detection of strong strain-rate sensitivity of yield strength, twinning, an FCC-to-BCC transformation, or yielding without vacancy-associated dislocation nucleation would falsify the hypothesis.
